newsitem.title: CHILE: EU vice-president Brittan to visit Chile.
newsitem.headline: EU vice-president Brittan to visit Chile.

text.p: European Union (EU) commission vice-president Sir Leon Brittan will make an official visit to Chile at the end of the month aimed at boosting trade ties, EU representative Kurt Juul said on Wednesday.

"Mr Brittan has heard a great deal about Chile as an emerging country," Juul told reporters after meeting Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza. "He is very interested in the seeing the reality of an emerging country in America."
Chile and the EU have signed an economic cooperation pact which Chile hopes eventually to extend to a full free trade agreement.
The bloc is one of Chile's largest trading partners with trade totalling $7.6 billion in 1995.

Brittan, who is in charge of the EU's trade relations, will arrive in Chile on March 28 on a private weekend visit to the far southern Patagonian region. He begins his four-day official visit on March 31 and then goes to Brazil.
